name: AP Physics 1
note: Unit and topic structure follows the College Board AP Physics 1 course framework (2024 revision). Titles and descriptions are written in Scorpio's own words; they are not College Board text.

units.title: Kinematics
units.summary: Describing motion in one and two dimensions with words, graphs, equations and vectors.

topics.title: Scalars and vectors in one dimension
topics.summary: Telling magnitude-only quantities from ones with direction, and using signs for direction along a line.

topics.title: Displacement, velocity and acceleration
topics.summary: Defining change in position, rate of change of position and rate of change of velocity; average versus instantaneous values.

topics.title: Representing motion
topics.summary: Moving between motion diagrams, position-time and velocity-time graphs and the constant-acceleration equations; slopes and areas.

topics.title: Reference frames and relative motion
topics.summary: How measured velocity depends on the observer, and adding velocities between frames.

topics.title: Vectors and motion in two dimensions
topics.summary: Splitting vectors into components and analysing projectiles with independent horizontal and vertical motion.

units.title: Force and translational dynamics
units.summary: Systems, forces and Newton's laws, including friction, springs, gravity and circular motion.

topics.title: Systems and center of mass
topics.summary: Choosing a system, telling internal from external forces, and locating the center of mass.

topics.title: Forces and free-body diagrams
topics.summary: Forces as interactions, and drawing every force on an object with correct direction and relative size.

topics.title: Newton's third law
topics.summary: Interaction pairs: equal in size, opposite in direction, acting on different objects.

topics.title: Newton's first law
topics.summary: Zero net force means constant velocity; inertia and equilibrium.

topics.title: Newton's second law
topics.summary: Net force equals mass times acceleration, applied to single objects and connected systems.

topics.title: Gravitational force
topics.summary: Universal gravitation, the gravitational field near a surface, and weight versus apparent weight.

topics.title: Kinetic and static friction
topics.summary: Sliding friction, the range of static friction up to its maximum, and coefficients of friction.

topics.title: Spring forces
topics.summary: Hooke's law: the restoring force of an ideal spring grows with stretch or compression.

topics.title: Circular motion
topics.summary: Centripetal acceleration and the real forces that provide it, including vertical circles and orbits.

units.title: Work, energy and power
units.summary: Energy stored and transferred in systems, work by forces, conservation of energy and power.

topics.title: Translational kinetic energy
topics.summary: Energy of motion, and how it depends on mass and the square of speed.

topics.title: Work
topics.summary: Energy transferred by a force over a displacement; sign of work, and work from force-displacement graphs.

topics.title: Potential energy
topics.summary: Energy stored in gravitational and spring interactions within a system, and the choice of zero.

topics.title: Conservation of energy
topics.summary: Total energy stays constant unless external work is done; tracking transfers with bar charts.

topics.title: Power
topics.summary: The rate of energy transfer, average and instantaneous.

units.title: Linear momentum
units.summary: Momentum, impulse, conservation of momentum and collisions.

topics.title: Linear momentum
topics.summary: Momentum as mass times velocity, a vector, for objects and systems.

topics.title: Change in momentum and impulse
topics.summary: Impulse equals change in momentum; average force over a time interval and force-time graphs.

topics.title: Conservation of linear momentum
topics.summary: With no net external force, a system's total momentum stays the same; center-of-mass velocity.

topics.title: Elastic and inelastic collisions
topics.summary: When kinetic energy is or is not conserved in a collision, and perfectly inelastic collisions.

units.title: Torque and rotational dynamics
units.summary: Rotational motion, torque, rotational inertia and Newton's laws for rotation.

topics.title: Rotational kinematics
topics.summary: Angular position, velocity and acceleration, and the constant angular acceleration equations.

topics.title: Connecting linear and rotational motion
topics.summary: Relating arc length, tangential speed and tangential acceleration to angular quantities through the radius.

topics.title: Torque
topics.summary: How a force's size, direction and lever arm about an axis produce a turning effect.

topics.title: Rotational inertia
topics.summary: Resistance to angular acceleration and its dependence on how mass is distributed; parallel-axis idea.

topics.title: Rotational equilibrium and Newton's first law in rotational form
topics.summary: Zero net torque and zero net force for objects at rest or rotating steadily.

topics.title: Newton's second law in rotational form
topics.summary: Net torque equals rotational inertia times angular acceleration, including pulleys with mass.

units.title: Energy and momentum of rotating systems
units.summary: Rotational kinetic energy, angular momentum and its conservation, rolling and orbits.

topics.title: Rotational kinetic energy
topics.summary: Energy of rotation and how it depends on rotational inertia and angular speed.

topics.title: Torque and work
topics.summary: Work done by a torque through an angular displacement.

topics.title: Angular momentum and angular impulse
topics.summary: Angular momentum of rigid bodies and point objects; angular impulse changes angular momentum.

topics.title: Conservation of angular momentum
topics.summary: With no net external torque, angular momentum stays the same as rotational inertia changes.

topics.title: Rolling
topics.summary: Rolling without slipping, splitting kinetic energy into translational and rotational parts.

topics.title: Motion of orbiting satellites
topics.summary: Circular and elliptical orbits, conservation of energy and angular momentum in orbits, and escape speed.

units.title: Oscillations
units.summary: Simple harmonic motion of springs and pendulums: period, graphs and energy.

topics.title: Defining simple harmonic motion
topics.summary: A restoring force proportional to displacement from equilibrium produces SHM.

topics.title: Frequency and period of SHM
topics.summary: What sets the period of a mass on a spring and of a simple pendulum, and what does not.

topics.title: Representing and analyzing SHM
topics.summary: Position, velocity and acceleration graphs and equations over a cycle.

topics.title: Energy of simple harmonic oscillators
topics.summary: Exchanges between kinetic and potential energy during an oscillation, and total energy versus amplitude.

units.title: Fluids
units.summary: Density, pressure, buoyancy and fluid flow.

topics.title: Internal structure and density
topics.summary: Density as mass per volume and ideal fluid assumptions.

topics.title: Pressure
topics.summary: Pressure as force per area, and how fluid pressure grows with depth; absolute and gauge pressure.

topics.title: Fluids and Newton's laws
topics.summary: Buoyant force from displaced fluid, floating and sinking, and free-body diagrams in fluids.

topics.title: Fluids and conservation of energy
topics.summary: The continuity equation and Bernoulli's equation for flowing fluids.
